[i]The Arelian State Broadcasting Corporation. Friday, April 17th 2028[/i]

Today, hundreds of thousands have gathered in city centres across the Union, as news broke that tens of thousands of civilians were murdered by the Romariian State. Questions are now being asked of the Romariian State, as they war against their own populace.

People are calling on the Government to act or intervene, as concern grows for the rightful Arels left in Geranora. 
But it proves well for the irredentist Violet March, as they seek restoration.

Parliament will decide on the 20th, as they discuss action. 
Tonight, vigils will take place, for all those lost.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Date Disclamer]
The Romariian Ordnungstaat, which is the main focus of this news, was founded on April 15th of 2028. The news report was created on April 18
[/spoiler]

Romariian News Network
---------------------------
Extremist Group arise in Nordlongum
---------------------------
After the brutal suppression of the Animist revolt in Yoshiland on April 12th, now known by the International World as the Yoshiland Massacre, and the rise of multiple riots across the nation, an Extremist group, called by its members as "Romariian Ordnungstaat", has been formed in the sparsely populated Nordlongum territory.

The founder of the Extremist group, Otto Dan Sigrid, stated that he formed the Romariian Ordnungstaat to replace Mario Mario's Government and promise equality and pride to its people.

The Actions of this group, however, do not match what Sigrid has stated, as the Romariian Ordnungstaat has used Terror attacks to expand its influence.

Experts warn, however, that due to the Yoshiland Massacre, more people may side with the opposition of the Romariian Government.

[list]──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[b]The first defeat has occurred for the Union Government.
[sub]Le gouvernement de l'Union a subi sa première défaite.[/b][/sub]
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────[/list]

[i][b]P I R N ─[/b][/i] On July 10, eighteen days after the [b]Union Government of Pirn[/b] declared a [b]Level 1 Federal Emergency[/b] on June 28, armed unrest broke out as a faction calling itself the [b]Second Pirn Republic[/b] or the Republic Restoration Front launched coordinated uprisings across parts of [b]Reine[/b], [b]Baria[/b], and [b]Rupert[/b]. Their stated aim: [i]to overthrow the newly established Union Government and restore the republican system.[/i]

The escalation has plunged Pirn into its most serious internal conflict since the civil strife following the [b]Pirn Conflict [i](19851990)[/i][/b]. While Union authorities still hold the upper hand overall, rebel forces have successfully seized large portions of Rupert Region, toppling several local administrations in the south and proclaiming the [b]Provisional Republican Government of Pirn[/b], the self-declared [b]Second Pirn Republic[/b]. The loss of territory is widely regarded as the first significant setback for the Union Government and loyalist regions. The governor of Rupert has been evacuated along with most civilians, though some residents were unable to flee and remain trapped behind rebel lines.

Prime Minister [b]Monica Franklin[/b] stated that her administration is seeking negotiations to allow civilians in occupied areas safe passage out of the conflict zone. [i]In the name of our Motherland Pirn, I will save our brothers and sisters held under the grip of terrorists,[/i] she told reporters.

Meanwhile, the uprisings in Baria and Reine have been largely contained, with several rebel commanders captured or killed. Despite the battlefield advantage held by the [b]Pirn Defence Force (PDF)[/b] and Union authorities, analysts warn that the loss of a large section of southern Rupert, including several small cities and towns, marks a critical failure in early government response.

Amid the ongoing fighting, casualty reports among civilians and local officials have begun to surface, and worryingly, foreign nationals are now among the dead. Unverified figures indicate at least 39 civilian fatalities, including three citizens of [nation=noflag]Stuipendia[/nation], along with one local government official. Images from the scene also show the [url=https://www.nationstates.net/nation=stuipendia]Stuipendian Consulate[/url] in [b]Chaepstow[/b], [b]Rupert Region[/b], reduced to ashes after being set ablaze by rebel fighters.

Conditions on the ground remain fluid, though accurate reporting has become increasingly difficult as journalists face direct threats from rebel groups, and some have already lost their lives in the conflict.

The afternoon light filtered softly through the tall windows of the imperial palace office. Emperor Alexander Karl von Halstern I sat in a high-backed chair, a glass of wine in hand, watching the steady stream of news reports playing on a polished screen across the room. 

A knock echoed at the heavy door.

Enter, the Emperor said without looking away from the screen.

The doors opened, and Prime Minister Moritz Jackman stepped inside with a respectful bow.

Your Imperial Majesty, Moritz began, straightening, I bring news regarding international correspondence.

Alexander lowered his glass slightly, finally turning his attention to the Prime Minister. Speak, Moritz. You seem pleased.

Moritz allowed a small smile. Indeed, Your Majesty. [nation]Hayan Dal[/nation] has formally granted permission for your yearly vacation to take place within their lands this year.

The Emperors eyebrows lifted, a faint smile forming.

They have also extended additional courtesies, Moritz continued. While you are there, they have expressed openness to a trade agreement. Furthermore, they have welcomed the opportunity for you to meet their leader in person.

Alexander leaned back slightly, clearly intrigued. A vacation and diplomacy combined, Great.

He took a measured sip of his wine, then set the glass down on the table beside him.

I accept, the Emperor said. It has been some time since I have traveled beyond our borders.

Moritz nodded. Shall I begin organizing the logistics immediately?

Of course, Alexander replied. Ensure the arrangements reflect the dignity of Tranvalia. Security, transport, diplomatic protocoleverything must be in order.

He stood slowly, adjusting his coat. While I am away, the State General will oversee governance as usual. I trust on it.

As always, Your Majesty, Moritz said. The administration will remain stable.

A brief pause settled between them before Alexander added, with a tone of quiet satisfaction, The companies and businessmen of Tranvalia will welcome this news. A new trade agreement will strengthen our economyand the people will celebrate another successful diplomatic step.

Moritz bowed again. I will ensure the announcement is prepared.

Alexander picked up his wine glass once more, taking another small sip.

Good, he said calmly. Then, after a brief moment, he looked back toward the Prime Minister. And Moritzwhen you make the arrangements, ask our hosts what they recommend. I would like to see their monuments and experience their food.

Moritz smiled, nodding. It will be done, Your Majesty.

Alexander gave a slight approving nod, returning his gaze toward the news as Moritz turned and quietly exited the chamber, the plans for the imperial journey now well underway.
